source.author: verg
source.text: Nate dea, nam te maioribus ire per altum auspiciis manifesta fides: sic fata deum rex sortitur, volvitque vices; is vertitur ordo pauca tibi e multis, quo tutior hospita lustres aequora et Ausonio possis considere portu, expediam dictis; prohibent nam cetera Parcae scire Helenum farique vetat Saturnia Iuno.
source.text_original: 'Nate dea, — nam te maioribus ire per altum / auspiciis manifesta fides: sic fata deum rex / sortitur, volvitque vices; is vertitur ordo — / pauca tibi e multis, quo tutior hospita lustres / aequora et Ausonio possis considere portu, / expediam dictis; prohibent nam cetera Parcae / scire Helenum farique vetat Saturnia Iuno.
source.text_english: Son of a goddess, for the clear proof that you are making your way over the deep under greater omens is this: the king of the gods thus determines the fates and turns their sequence. That order is changed. I will explain a few things to you from among many, so that you may sail more safely over the foreign seas and be able to settle in an Ausonian harbor. For the Parcae forbid me to know the rest, and Saturnian Juno forbids Helenus to speak.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: hunc ferus Aeetes, Scythiam Phasimque rigentem qui colit heu magni Solis pudor, hospita vina nil nostri divumque memor.
reuse.text_original: hunc ferus Aeetes, Scythiam Phasimque rigentem / qui colit (heu magni Solis pudor), hospita vina / nil nostri divumque memor.
reuse.text_english: This man, the savage Aeetes, who inhabits Scythia and the frozen Phasis, alas, the shame of great Sol, mindful of neither us nor the gods, had no regard for hospitality or wine.
